entry.issue_paraphrase: Converting ECDSA signatures between the raw (r||s) and DER (ASN.1) encodings crashes or corrupts memory when the caller supplies a curve bit size larger than the biggest curve the library supports (521 bits). The conversion routine copies each coordinate into a fixed-size internal stack buffer that only fits the largest supported curve, without checking the size of the incoming value, so a 544-bit value overflows the buffer. On hardened glibc builds the process is aborted with a buffer-overflow error; without that protection the stack is silently corrupted and the routine returns a misleading status or crashes later.
entry.fix_summary: mbedtls_ecdsa_raw_to_der() and mbedtls_ecdsa_der_to_raw() now verify that the coordinate length (PSA_BITS_TO_BYTES(bits)) fits their fixed-size local buffers (MBEDTLS_ECP_MAX_BYTES) before copying, returning MBEDTLS_ERR_ASN1_BUF_TOO_SMALL instead of overflowing the stack.
entry.notes: Security fix (CVE-2024-45157): the advisory title itself hints at the two functions, so the paraphrase above deliberately omits the function names. The test cases have no depends_on guard, so they always run; the rest of the suite (43 cases) passes untouched. Suite compiles in under a minute and runs in seconds; library build is the long pole (~2 min at -j8, ~15-20 min at 1 CPU). Fail-at-parent is deterministic on Ubuntu 24.04 gcc due to FORTIFY_SOURCE.

entry.issue_paraphrase: Z3's fused multiply-add `fp.fma` can round a result one unit in the last place (ulp) away from the true IEEE 754 value for binary16 (`(_ FloatingPoint 5 11)`) operands. In the cases affected, the result of `fp.fma RNE x y x` with all operands given as fixed bit patterns and a fixed rounding mode is not the correct rounded encoding: a query asserting the exact IEEE encoding equals the expected value is answered `sat`, meaning the solver computed a different (wrong) encoding. The wrong rounding appears on the path where the intermediate product needs a sticky-bit reduction for the second rounding step, making some inexact results look like exact ties.
entry.fix_summary: In fpa2bv_converter::mk_fma, the h2 rounding path computed sticky_h2 (extract of the discarded low bits) but erroneously reduced sticky_h1 (the h1 discarded-bit range) when building sticky_h2_red, so one sticky bit was dropped and some inexact products rounded as exact ties. Fix changes that one zero-extended BREDOR input from sticky_h1 to sticky_h2; the h1 path is untouched.
entry.notes: Deterministic, no network needed. The repro must use `(check-sat-using (then fpa2bv simplify bit-blast smt))` exactly as the project's own regression test does (forces the fpa2bv conversion path). Golden unit test: new block in src/test/smt_context.cpp (module `smt_context`) asserting l_false with the fpa2bv->simplify->bit-blast->smt pipeline. The fix itself is a one-line variable swap, but locating it requires reading the fp.fma conversion code. Build cost is the only heavy step (~5 min at 64 cores, order of 30-60 min at 1 CPU).

entry.issue_paraphrase: Padding a string to a very large target size can exhaust the Java heap and kill the whole process instead of returning the input unchanged. Passing Integer.MIN_VALUE as the desired length makes the padding routines subtract the current string length from that minimum int, which overflows into a huge positive pad count; the code then attempts to materialize a multi-gigabyte character array and the JVM dies with an OutOfMemoryError that no application code can catch. Any server that pads values based on untrusted lengths crashes outright, where a size no larger than the string's own length should simply be a no-op returning the original string.
entry.fix_summary: leftPad and rightPad (both the char-padChar and String-padStr overloads) now return the input string immediately when the requested size is not greater than the current string length, so the pad-count arithmetic can never overflow into a giant allocation. Previously only the str == null case was short-circuited. Added regression asserts calling leftPad("abc", Integer.MIN_VALUE, ...) and rightPad(...) expecting the string unchanged.
entry.notes: DoS/OOM class bug, very user-visible, public StringUtils API. The parent-side failure is an uncaught OutOfMemoryError that crashes the fork, which makes the golden test run report a surefire dump + mvn exit 1 rather than an ordinary assertion failure - do not mistake that for an environment problem. Keep the direct repro under -Xmx256m so the OOM is fast and deterministic. The `mvn test-compile` before the direct repro builds target/classes for the checkout being tested. Test runs are offline; only the first maven invocation needs network.

entry.issue_paraphrase: Dependency names declared in the PEP 621 style of a Python pyproject.toml are recorded exactly as typed (e.g. 'Flask' instead of 'flask', 'typing_extensions' instead of 'typing-extensions', 'ruamel.yaml' instead of 'ruamel-yaml'), so the names do not line up with the normalized names produced by other Python lockfiles. A package can therefore be reported under different spellings in different parts of the same scan, breaking dependency-name matching between the project manifest and the lockfile.
entry.fix_summary: The PEP 621 'dependencies' name extraction now passes each parsed name through python.NormalizePkgName(name, true) (PEP 503 normalization: lowercase, runs of non-alphanumerics -> '-') before storing it in the dependency set, matching the normalization the poetry/pylock parsers already apply; the fixture now uses non-normalized spellings to prove the match.
entry.notes: Small fix (2 source lines) but a real, user-visible correctness bug with the project's own regression coverage. Same env caveats as the other entries (GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2, single-module `go test`, ~1GB first download). Verification logs in container trivy-miner: /tmp/pyp_parent.log and /tmp/pyp_fix.log.

entry.issue_paraphrase: A Python version file (`.python-version` or `.python-versions`) whose entries carry leading or trailing whitespace - for example lines like " python3.12 " or entries separated by tabs - causes uv to silently ignore those entries. Instead of being read as version requests, the padded lines are treated as unsupported executable names, a warning is printed for each, and the requested Python version is never selected, so commands that depend on the pin pick a different interpreter or fail. A version file that is perfectly valid except for incidental indentation behaves as if it were empty, and the only hint is a warning that the request is 'unsupported'.
entry.fix_summary: Trim each line of the version file before filtering comments and parsing: `content.lines().map(str::trim).filter(...).map(PythonRequest::parse)` (replacing a per-line `line.trim()` inside the comment check on the raw line), so padded entries parse as version requests, and drops an intermediate allocation. Extends the `python_pin_with_comments` integration test (renamed python_pin_with_comments_and_whitespace) to cover spaces, tabs, whitespace-only lines and indented comments for both version-file names.

entry.issue_paraphrase: Sanitizing a live DOM subtree in place can abort part-way through when the root element shadows the document property the cleaner reads to build its traversal, for example a form element whose own property lookup is intercepted by a child element named after that property. The exception escapes before the cleanup barrier runs, so the caller gets control back with event-handler attributes still attached to surviving descendants of the tree that was supposed to be scrubbed. The same in-place sanitization on an un-shadowed element completes and strips such handlers normally.
entry.fix_summary: Read ownerDocument through the cached Node.prototype getter (immune to own-property shadowing / LegacyOverrideBuiltIns clobbers) in _createNodeIterator and _scrubTemplateExpressions, moved iterator construction inside the fail-closed exception barrier, and added a helper that forks the hook-mutable allowlist off its shared binding before lazily-installed uponSanitize* hooks can mutate it. Regression tests use an own accessor to reproduce the clobber in any engine and assert the armed handler is gone whether the call returns or fails closed.

entry.issue_paraphrase: When two IMAP URLs are fetched in a single curl invocation and their mailbox paths differ only in letter case, the second request silently skips the re-selection step and runs its fetch against the mailbox that was selected for the first request. Case is significant to IMAP servers, so 'Private' and 'private' can be completely different folders, yet the client assumes they are the same and never issues the second SELECT command. As a result, mail is read from the wrong folder without any error or warning being reported, and only the raw command transcript (or a strict server) reveals that the wrong mailbox was addressed. Mixed-case folder names on the same server connection are sufficient to trigger it.
entry.fix_summary: imap_perform() now compares the requested mailbox with the connection's currently selected mailbox case-sensitively (with an explicit case-insensitive exception only for 'INBOX'), so a case-differing mailbox name forces a new SELECT before the FETCH. test804 was updated to request 'Private' then 'private' and verify two SELECT commands on the wire.
entry.notes: Fully offline: the standalone repro needs only the small python IMAP server (approximately 50 lines, included in the reproduction field of this entry's verification above; the harness's ftpserver.pl is a reference implementation of the needed responses). The task must assert on the server-side transcript (count of SELECT commands), not on curl's exit code (0 in both directions). Golden test 804 needs the harness build and an 'imap' server - runtests.pl starts one automatically from tests/ftpserver.pl. Compare with real case differences in the mailbox; identical names must still reuse the selection, so a naive 'always SELECT' fix is wrong.

entry.issue_paraphrase: The printf/format %c conversion writes its argument's low byte verbatim, so formatting a codepoint above 127 produces a string containing invalid UTF-8 bytes. entry.issue_paraphrase: The per-client timeout is silently ignored when a request is created directly as an httpx.Request instance instead of through the client's own request builder: sending a manually constructed request via client.send(...) runs with the default timeout even though the client was configured with a much smaller one, so operations that should be aborted almost immediately instead hang for the full default period and eventually succeed anyway. entry.issue_paraphrase: spaCy 3.8+ added a context-manager API for bounding memory usage when processing large volumes of text: entering a memory zone makes all new vocabulary strings and lexemes transient, and leaving the zone frees them. But if an exception is raised inside the with-block, the cleanup that should restore normal vocabulary memory never runs. Afterwards the vocabulary permanently reports that it is still inside a memory zone, words created during the failed block are either leaked or freed at the wrong time, and further lookups and additions can crash or corrupt the vocabulary. Anyone catching an exception around a memory zone (for example a server processing documents under a memory budget) is left with a corrupted, unusable vocabulary.
entry.fix_summary: Wrapped the `yield mem` in both `Vocab.memory_zone` and `StringStore.memory_zone` in try/finally so the transient-string cleanup and the memory-pool reset always run even when an exception propagates through the context manager. New regression test test_memory_zone_exception_cleanup asserts the vocab is not stuck in zone state and transient words are removed after an exception.

entry.issue_paraphrase: Setting the response status code to an invalid value is silently accepted: codes below 100 or above 999, non-integers like 200.1, a numeric string such as "200", NaN, or undefined are all stored as the response status without complaint. The request then completes with a wrong, unparseable, or meaningless status line - clients observe e.g. 200 OK where an error was intended - instead of failing immediately with a clear message. Invalid status codes should be rejected with an explicit error as soon as they are set.

entry.issue_paraphrase: psutil's process iterator silently omits zombie processes from the list it yields, even though zombies are still present in the OS process table and remain fully queryable through the direct process-handle API. Any code that enumerates processes to monitor, kill, or aggregate them misses these entries, and the iterator's internal cache even forgets them as if they had disappeared, so the omission repeats on every call.
entry.fix_summary: process_iter() adds an explicit `except ZombieProcess:` branch before `except NoSuchProcess:` that yields the process instead of dropping it (ZombieProcess is a subclass of NoSuchProcess, so the generic handler was swallowing it). entry.issue_paraphrase: Running `git fetch --multiple --jobs=0` crashes git with an internal BUG diagnostic ('BUG: ... you must provide a non-zero number of processes!') and an abort signal rather than doing anything useful. The documented behavior for a parallel fetch setting of 0 is to fall back to a sensible default (the number of CPUs), which also used to be the behavior of `--jobs=0`; after a refactor it started aborting instead. The command should succeed using the default parallelism.
entry.fix_summary: cmd_fetch() now treats --jobs=0 like fetch.parallel=0: `if (!max_jobs) max_jobs = online_cpus();` before running the parallel fetch machinery, so run_processes_parallel is never called with 0 processes. Root cause: 51243f9 (2022-10) removed the online_cpus fallback for explicit 0 values.

entry.issue_paraphrase: Splitting a string with a regular expression that is capable of zero-width matches - like a word boundary or a lookahead/lookbehind - can silently drop the final character (or the entire string) from the result. A single-character input split on a word boundary comes back as an empty list instead of a one-element list, and a string like 'foo' split on lookarounds that should produce f, o, o comes back as f, o. The JDK's own String.split handles the same patterns correctly, so users switching between the two APIs get different results, and any code relying on the split output loses the last token without an error.
entry.fix_summary: PatternSplitter's empty-match handling changes 'if (offset >= toSplit.length()) offset = -1;' to 'if (offset > toSplit.length()) offset = -1;'. Previously, when a zero-width match occurred exactly at the final position of the string, iteration stopped without a final separator search, so the trailing substring (the last character, or the whole string when the input is a single character) was dropped. With the relaxed condition the iterator does one more separatorStart() round, finds the end-of-string zero-width match, and emits the final token.

entry.issue_paraphrase: When a superclass declared in a different package defines a test method, and a subclass declares a method with the same name and parameter list, the framework treats the inherited package-private method as overridden even though Java visibility rules mean it is not an override. As a result, the superclass's package-private test method is silently skipped, and only the subclass's method is discovered and executed. Tests that used to run therefore disappear from the results without any error or warning as soon as a subclass adds a method with the same signature.
entry.fix_summary: Method selection was reworked so that a discovered method is always reported against the class that actually declares it. ClassSelectorResolver.selectMethod now builds a new DeclaredMethodSelector carrying the full list of candidate classes; MethodSelectorResolver/MethodSegmentResolver use it to resolve the declaring class via ReflectionUtils.findDeclaredMethods instead of the deleted MethodFinder heuristic (which decomposed the method segment and picked a single class). MethodSelector grew constructor/logic support for this. Net effect: a package-private superclass method in another package plus an unrelated same-signature subclass method are now both discovered and executed (with the same display name).
entry.notes: Both golden tests are integration-style (JUnit Platform launcher + testkit) but completely offline. Class-level --tests filter used. First run per tree downloads gradle 9.2.0 and builds the jupiter-tests dependency graph (~3 min); subsequent runs seconds. The two displayed statistic assertions make this a robust oracle. The commit message references PR #5100 but the underlying issue it fixes is #5098.

entry.issue_paraphrase: gzip streams that carry an FEXTRA extra field, as produced by BGZF and other tools that store metadata in the gzip header, cannot be decompressed: decoding throws a decompression failure and the stream is rejected, even though the same bytes decompress cleanly with the JDK's own gzip reader. The decoder reads the header's extra-field length into a value that is guaranteed to stay at its 'no extra field' sentinel by the way it is accumulated, so the extra bytes are never skipped and are handed to the inflater as if they were compressed data. Corrected handling also reads the two-byte length in the wrong byte order. Ordinary gzip output never sets this flag, which is why only unusual-but-valid producers are affected; a secondary symptom is that concatenated gzip members can contaminate each other's header parsing when the first member has an extra field.
entry.fix_summary: JdkZlibDecoder now assembles the gzip XLEN field as a little-endian assignment ('xlen = xlen2 << 8 | xlen1;') instead of OR-ing a big-endian value into the -1 sentinel, and resets xlen to -1 when a new gzip member starts so a first-stream extra field cannot leak into the next member's header parsing. Adds JdkZlibTest.testGZIPDecodeWithExtraField and testConcatenatedGzipFirstStreamHasExtraField, which craft the FEXTRA stream by hand and sanity-check it with GZIPInputStream.
entry.notes: Fully offline and deterministic: fixtures are hand-crafted gzip byte arrays validated with JDK GZIPInputStream inside the test; EmbeddedChannel keeps everything in-process. Both golden tests fail at parent, either alone gives the fail/pass signal. Same build notes as the other codec-compression entry: closure common, buffer, transport, codec-base, testsuite-common; first reactor build absorbs ~5 min of one-time Maven Central downloads, observed compile of the closure ~40s at -T16 on a 64-core host, per-state single-module incremental ~5-10s at default parallelism. No dependency pins (pure JDK). Latent-in-the-codebase bug (GZIPOutputStream never emits FEXTRA), so it is genuinely undiscoverable by just running the pre-existing suite at parent.

entry.issue_paraphrase: If a monkeypatch mutation fails — for instance setitem or delitem on an immutable mapping proxy, or delattr of an attribute that cannot be deleted (such as a slot attribute on a class) — pytest still records an undo entry for the operation that never happened. Calling undo() afterwards then re-raises the original error (TypeError or AttributeError) instead of being a harmless no-op, and the rollback bookkeeping no longer reflects what was actually changed. Failed mutations should register nothing to undo.
entry.fix_summary: MonkeyPatch.delattr, setitem and delitem now capture the old value first and append the undo entry to self._setattr / self._setitem only after the mutation itself (delattr / dict-style assignment / del) succeeded, so a failed mutation leaves no stale undo record and undo() is a no-op.

entry.issue_paraphrase: A constructor called through a parameter that is annotated as the type object of a TypeVar, e.g. `Type[T]`, is rejected by mypy whenever T's bound is a union of classes: every call site reports 'Incompatible return value type (got "Union[A, B]", expected "T")' even though both classes are instantiable with the same arguments. The constructed value's precise type is inferred correctly — mypy itself reveals it as the individual class — but the check against the TypeVar's declared return type fails anyway, so otherwise valid factory functions are littered with errors. The failure appears in both the no-argument and the one-argument call forms.
entry.fix_summary: ExpressionChecker.analyze_type_type_callee handles a Type[T] call by finding the constructor of each possible type; the return types of those constructors must be replaced with the TypeVar instance T. The fix extracts that substitution into replace_type_type_callee_ret_type and makes it recurse into UnionType items (after get_proper_type and .relevant_items()), so a union-bounded TypeVar yields a union of constructors whose return types are all replaced. A regression case asserts the two revealed types and that no errors are raised; a match-statement case in check-python310.test is updated accordingly.
entry.notes: Fast (~2s CLI, ~3.5s golden pytest run) and fully offline. Note the fix also updates an EXPECTED reveal in test-data/unit/check-python310.test (reveal of choice() in the default match arm changes from 'b.One | b.Two' to 'T_Choice`-1'), so overlaying the fix's test files at the parent is the correct golden procedure; at parent only the new case testTypeUsingTypeCConstructorReturnFromTypeVarUnionBound fails. mypy runtime needs librt+ast-serialize wheels (cp312 available). Use -k-filtered pytest runs.

entry.issue_paraphrase: After trimming a stream and then lowering its total entry counter, existing consumer groups keep reporting a read position higher than the stream's counter: group information shows a negative lag, and a database snapshot taken at that point can no longer be loaded back into the server, so restarts, failovers and backups break. Lowering the stream's counter should also pull the groups' read positions back so the snapshot stays loadable.
entry.fix_summary: In xsetidCommand, when ENTRIESADDED lowers entries_added below its previous value, clamp every consumer group's entries_read down to the new entries_added (skipping SCG_INVALID_ENTRIES_READ), matching what XGROUP CREATE/SETID already do, so the entries_read <= entries_added invariant holds and saved RDBs remain loadable.

entry.issue_paraphrase: A regex in which the first alternative is optional can report a match that starts too late on the haystack. entry.issue_paraphrase: Deserializing an adjacently tagged enum - an enum that is represented as a map containing one key for the variant tag and one key for the content - fails whenever the map also holds any other, unrelated keys. The deserializer treats the first key that is neither the tag nor the content as a hard error, so maps produced by other sources that carry extra metadata fields cannot be parsed at all, even though unknown fields are silently ignored everywhere else in the library. When the strict deny-unknown-fields option is set, those extra keys should instead be rejected deliberately, and when it is not set they should be skipped transparently.
entry.fix_summary: Added a TagContentOtherField visitor that classifies each map key as tag, content or other; generated deserialization code for adjacently tagged enums now loops, skipping and consuming 'other' keys (values read via IgnoredAny) until the tag/content keys are found, when deny_unknown_fields is unset. When deny_unknown_fields is set it keeps using the strict visitor that errors on any other key, so the option is now actually honored instead of being the universal behavior.

entry.issue_paraphrase: Solving a system of equations in which one equation involves the sign function crashes with a low-level arithmetic TypeError (something like 'unsupported operand type(s) for /: Integer and Interval'), because the equation sign(x) - 1 = 0 is turned into an interval of x values that the solver then tries to divide other expressions by. Instead of the crash the call should either produce the solution or fail with a clear solver-level error, and a lone sign equation should still yield a proper answer set rather than being reported as an unsolvable condition set.
entry.fix_summary: In _solve_using_known_values (used by nonlinsolve), once one equation has given a solution for a variable the solver combined it with solveset_complex of another equation and kept going, and later died of a raw TypeError when that accumulated solution was an Interval (as produced by sign(x)-1=0). The fix raises NotImplementedError immediately after the combine step when the result is not a FiniteSet/ImageSet/ConditionSet/Union/EmptySet, and narrows the except clause to only ValueError so an introduced NotImplementedError propagates instead of being silently swallowed and re-attempted. Result: a clear 'nonlinsolve cannot handle solution of type Interval' error instead of the crash, and the single sign equation now returns a FiniteSet.
entry.notes: No network needed at test time. Whole verification (both directions plus golden test) takes about 2-3 minutes at 1 CPU. Run only the single nodeid 'sympy/solvers/tests/test_solveset.py::test_nonlinsolve_sign'; the whole test_solveset.py module takes many minutes. The golden test requires the fix's semantics (NotImplementedError for the two-equation cases, FiniteSet for the single case); a naive implementation that only special-cases the sign function in a different place can still satisfy it, which is fine for a task. sympy prints a 'DO *NOT* COMMIT!' banner via conftest at pytest startup; harmless. The lint/doctest addopts in pyproject.toml do not affect the marked node.

entry.issue_paraphrase: Nodes running up-to-date Syncthing send block-data requests with a zero byte count (for empty files), but the receiving node treats any request size of zero as a protocol violation: the dispatcher terminates the connection with an error instead of replying. entry.fix_summary: Two-part fix. lib/protocol/protocol.go: dispatcherLoop now rejects only strictly negative request sizes (msg.Size < 0), accepting the zero-sized requests current versions actually send; lib/model/folder_sendrecv.go: copierRoutine and pullerRoutine skip zero-size blocks as no-ops instead of running them through the limiter/request path, and TestPullCtxCancel uses Size:42 so it still exercises the cancellation path.
entry.notes: Regression test uses the in-package in-memory connection harness (testutil.NewBlockingRW/NoopRW), no real sockets or network. Watch out: the branch condition is symmetric and easy to 'fix' wrongly (rejecting negatives only vs accepting zero) - TestRequestZeroSize requires the rawConnection to actually reply to a size-0 request. Golden test lives in lib/protocol/protocol_test.go which also contains TestRequestMaxSize (requires MaxRequestSize const, already present at the parent). lib/model changes are not exercised by the golden test; do not require lib/model tests as they are slower (~minutes to compile) and some need real folder setups.

entry.issue_paraphrase: For projects managed by a pnpm release that writes its YAML lockfile as multiple documents - the first holding the package manager's own environment (pnpm itself and its per-platform binary packages), a later one the actual project dependencies - the scanner decodes only the first document, so it reports the package manager's internal packages as if they were the project's dependencies, flooding the SBOM with pnpm's machinery while the real project dependency is missing from the report.
entry.fix_summary: The pnpm YAML parser now loops over all YAML documents, skipping any document that is the pnpm environment lockfile (detected via the new isEnvLockfile() on the lockfile's importers, which checks for configDependencies/packageManagerDependencies fields) and parsing the first non-environment document; an empty/env-only file returns no packages.

entry.issue_paraphrase: URL decoding with plus-to-space conversion disabled mishandles a literal plus sign when it is immediately followed by two hexadecimal digits: it is treated as a percent-encoding escape and replaced by the decoded byte. A timestamp with a UTC offset such as '+00:00' in a path therefore injects a NUL byte into the decoded value. Only the compiled (accelerated) code path is affected; the pure-Python behavior is correct.
entry.fix_summary: In the Cython implementation of uri.decode, handle b'+' explicitly: only translate it to a space when unquote_plus is enabled, otherwise copy it through and never let it fall into the percent-decoding branch.
entry.notes: REPRODUCIBILITY DEPENDS ON THE COMPILED EXTENSION. (a) pip install falcon from PyPI installs a prebuilt wheel that includes the affected compiled module, so a task pinned to a released buggy falcon would reproduce out of the box; (b) installing from source is pure-Python on bench-base:python-3.12 unless gcc + Cython are installed first — the direct repro then fails with ImportError pretending the bug is gone. If authoring from source, the image must install gcc (and Cython) first. The golden test runs the str variant through the pure-Python path (passes even at parent); only bytearray/join_list variants of test_uri_decode_unquote_plus fail at parent. Use the direct-repro assertion (decode('+00', unquote_plus=False) == '+00') as the oracle string, not the pytest selection alone.

entry.issue_paraphrase: Asking an undirected graph built with the GraphBuilder API for its set of edges can return a set that violates the standard Collection contract: the set claims to contain an EndpointPair whose endpoints were passed in ordered form, but none of the pairs actually in the set equals that ordered pair. Code that relies on contains() to mean 'an equal element is present' - for example iterating the set to find the matching pair - therefore fails or returns nothing, and the same inconsistency appears across the graph/network APIs whenever an ordered endpoint pair is used with an undirected graph. The behavior is also asymmetric: on directed graphs the pair types are rejected, but on undirected graphs they slip through and produce these false-positive membership results.
entry.fix_summary: EndpointPair ordering is now checked symmetrically: AbstractBaseGraph.isOrderingCompatible and AbstractNetwork.isOrderingCompatible change from 'endpoints.isOrdered() || !this.isDirected()' to 'endpoints.isOrdered() == this.isDirected()', so an undirected graph rejects ordered EndpointPairs (and a directed graph rejects unordered ones) with IllegalArgumentException(ENDPOINTS_MISMATCH); GraphConstants.ENDPOINTS_MISMATCH's message was generalized ('endpoints' ordering is not compatible with directionality of the graph') to cover both directions. AdjacentNode, edges/incidentEdges, hasEdgeConnecting(EndpointPair), edgeValueOrDefault(EndpointPair), putEdgeValue(EndpointPair,...) and the Network equivalents now refuse or correctly report the mismatched pair instead of returning false positives; the test suite's assertions were inverted to match (e.g. hasEdgeConnecting_undirected_mismatch now expects false, and edgesConnecting/edgeConnectingOrNull expect the exception).
entry.notes: Newest entry (May 2022, guava 31.x era) and the only graph-package one; adds era diversity alongside the 2016 (Splitter), 2019 (ImmutableSet) and 2020 (ByteSource) fixes. Direct repro needs just guava/src (graph + base + collect + primitives) compiled with javac; no test framework at runtime. Caveat: this is a deliberate API behavior tightening (ordered pairs on undirected graphs go from silently accepted to rejected/false), so the task instruction must be phrased around the observable contract violation (contains() returning true with no equal element) rather than 'make the tests pass on new behavior', because at the fix commit existing user code calling putEdgeValue(EndpointPair.ordered(...)) on an undirected graph will start throwing. The golden classes live in the big graph test-suite hierarchy (AbstractGraphTest etc. in guava-testlib), which I did not compile; a task built on this entry should use the direct repro (or the small EndpointPairTest.endpointPair_undirected_contains method, which only needs the graph test dir + testlib) as the oracle.

entry.issue_paraphrase: Group betweenness centrality can return a nonzero score for a group of nodes even though no shortest path between any two nodes outside the group passes through the group's interior, where the mathematically correct score is zero. entry.fix_summary: Change the 'has no path through group' term (dvxy) so the denominator uses the group-aware path counts sigma_m[v][y] (and sigma_m[x][y]) instead of the all-pairs sigma, and add an explicit guard skipping the update when sigma_m[x][y], sigma_m[x][v] or sigma_m[v][y] is 0, so the crossing-rate is 0 when no path goes through the group.

entry.issue_paraphrase: When formatting TypeScript interfaces and object types, Prettier drops the quotes from a method literally named 'new': `"new"(id: string): number` is rewritten as `new(id: string): number`. In TypeScript an unquoted new(...) inside an interface is a construct signature (it describes how to build instances), not a method named new - so the reformatted source has a different type-level meaning than the original. The quotes on a method named new should be preserved instead of removed.
entry.fix_summary: isKeySafeToUnquote in src/language-js/print/key.js returns false for TSMethodSignature nodes whose key value is 'new', so the quote-props machinery never unquotes that name (the same name printed via a different AST node type is still subject to the normal quote rules).

entry.issue_paraphrase: The names of the artifacts setuptools produces — source-distribution archives and the .egg-info directory component derived from the project's full name — lose version information: the version is rewritten into a canonicalized shorthand before being put into the file name, so a project that declares version '1.0' gets archives named with '1', and a project with no explicit version (default '0.0.0') gets archives named with '0'. The file names then disagree with the full version string recorded inside the metadata, which breaks release tooling, artifact matching and users reading the artifacts.
entry.fix_summary: Distribution.get_fullname() (patched in from setuptools/_core_metadata.py) stopped running the version through packaging.utils.canonicalize_version and now embeds self.get_version() verbatim, so artifact names keep the user's version string exactly (the canonical_name part for the project name was already fine). Closes #4302 (and #3593).
entry.notes: 100% offline. Direct repro is a single python invocation (import setuptools triggers the monkey-patch that installs this get_fullname). entry.issue_paraphrase: When a git dependency is specified by an explicit ref such as refs/heads/somebranch or refs/tags/v1.0, poetry's legacy clone routine runs `git checkout` with the raw ref unchanged instead of with the plain branch or tag name. entry.fix_summary: Git._clone_legacy() called revision.replace('refs/head/', '') twice without assigning the result (so no stripping ever happened) and used the misspelled refs/head/ path; fixed by assigning revision = revision.removeprefix('refs/heads/') and revision = revision.removeprefix('refs/tags/') before SystemGit.checkout.

entry.fix_summary: One line in torchvision/transforms/v2/functional/_augment.py::jpeg_image: change `image.view((-1,) + image.shape[-3:])` to `image.reshape(...)` so non-contiguous leading dimensions are copied instead of rejected. entry.issue_paraphrase: Searching with a pattern that contains a Unicode word boundary can return a match that is too short when the haystack contains non-ASCII characters and a literal-driven fast search path is selected. For example, a pattern that matches one or more characters, then a word boundary, then a newline, searched against a haystack like 'β77\n', is reported as matching only 3..5 instead of the full 0..5, so callers receive a truncated match whose start offset is wrong and capture spans that do not align with the true match. A full, valid match exists at the very beginning of the haystack, so the search should return that one.
entry.fix_summary: In the meta engine's ad hoc DFA search routines (meta/limited.rs and meta/stopat.rs: dfa/hybrid half-reverse searches and end-of-input handling), always return a MatchError::quit when a quit state is entered, even if a match was tentatively found before the quit. Previously the routines returned the tentative match, which produced too-short offsets when Unicode word boundaries forced a quit. Returning the error lets the higher-level engine divert to a strategy that can handle Unicode word boundaries correctly.
entry.notes: Test is a data-driven entry in testdata/regression.toml executed by the repo-root integration test 'suite_string::default' (test target is named 'integration' at this commit; it is renamed 'suite_string' in current HEAD). The suite run takes <1 s after build; the same toml entry is checked by several suites (string, bytes, set, nfa, backtrack), the string default one is the golden direction. REGEX_TEST env var filters data tests (per harness output). No committed Cargo.lock; fresh crates.io resolution builds with stable rustc 1.98. Ubuntu 24.04 apt rustc (1.75) is too old if dependency resolution picks newer crates.

entry.issue_paraphrase: The robust-fitting routine can compute a nonsensical, non-positive budget for the maximum number of random trials when a very small target probability or a large minimum sample count makes one of the logarithms underflow to one. The computed trial count must be guaranteed to be a positive number.

entry.issue_paraphrase: The trust-region family of minimizers (e.g. trust-exact) evaluates the objective, gradient and Hessian at a proposed trial point before deciding whether to accept the step, and treats a NaN objective at the trial point as an ordinary value. When the objective is only defined on part of the domain, optimization aborts with an exception thrown by an out-of-domain Hessian evaluation instead of rejecting the step and shrinking the search radius, and domain-undefined (NaN) trial values are not handled as rejections either.
entry.fix_summary: Moved the local-model construction to after the trial point is accepted, evaluating the raw objective at the candidate first, and maps NaN objective values at trial points to +inf so the step is rejected and the trust radius shrinks (also cutting wasted Hessian evaluations on rejected steps).
entry.notes: Pure-Python, 26-line delta; requires understanding the trust-region accept/reject iteration. entry.issue_paraphrase: When an ORM-enabled UPDATE statement that uses RETURNING is executed with the option that re-fetches changed objects from the database after the statement, the first execution returns correct values but on the next execution of an equivalent statement the returned columns are mislabeled: looking up a column object returns the value of a different column, so for example the value of the last RETURNING column is returned where the first was requested. The corruption occurs when the order of the columns in the .returning() clause differs from the order of the columns as declared on the mapped table, and it appears on any execution served from the ORM's compiled statement cache.
entry.fix_summary: In _BulkUDCompileState._or_create_orm_setting (ORM bulk UPDATE/DELETE compile state), the ORM's load execution options (which include a flag disabling result-level adapt_to_context) are now merged into the effective execution options that are part of the cached construct. On a cache hit the ORM UPDATE/DELETE RETURNING statement is a 'two level' statement whose cached core level returns columns in mapper order while the ORM level carries the user's .returning() order; skipping the positional core adaptation keeps the cursor keymap consistent (Column-object index == string-name index) across cache hits.
entry.notes: No external DB needed (sqlite supports UPDATE..RETURNING). Both golden tests run in ~0.05s. Only the [update] variant discriminates; an author should target CacheAdaptReturningOrderTest::test_returning_keymap_stable_across_cache_hit[update]. The direct repro checks result.raw (the underlying core result) because ORM-level row access re-processes positions and can mask the corruption. Requires sqlite >= 3.35 (Python 3.12 bundles 3.4x).

entry.issue_paraphrase: A modulo expression inside another modulo can silently change when integer-typed symbols are involved: if a symbol is declared integer, simplifying an expression such as (2 * (x mod 3)) mod 5 squares the inner residue, producing a different expression than the same code with an ordinary symbol. Comparing the two forms after normalizing the symbol gives inequality even though they describe the same arithmetic, and a second family built with floor shows the same discrepancy. The integer assumption is supposed to only add simplifications, never alter the value.
entry.fix_summary: In Mod.number_eval, the list of non-mod factors was rebuilt by iterating over p.args and reducing only the Integer factors, so factors of p that were themselves Mod expressions were duplicated into BOTH the mod list and the non-mod list; with p containing an integer-assumed symbol both copies survived, which made the inner Mod appear twice (squared). The fix iterates over the already-filtered non_mod_l list so Mod factors are not duplicated. (.mailmap change in the same commit is irrelevant.)

entry.issue_paraphrase: Restarting a pane's command with respawn-pane while a control-mode client is attached and behind on that pane's output can make the entire tmux server die a few seconds later: client commands start reporting that the server is gone and the session is lost. entry.fix_summary: Add control_reset_pane() and call it from spawn_pane() for all control clients when a pane is respawned: drop any output still queued for control clients from the old buffer and reset each client's and the pane's offsets (used/base/pipe) to the fresh empty buffer, preventing control clients from reading past the end of the new buffer and crashing the server in input_parse.

entry.issue_paraphrase:
Reading a CSV file whose lines end with the '
' sequence (common output of certain Windows tools) using the parallel CSV reader can silently return more rows than the file actually contains: rows near buffer boundaries get counted twice, so a 10,000-row file yields 10,002 rows while the sequential reader returns exactly 10,000. Parallel and sequential scans of the same file must agree on the row count.
entry.fix_summary: In StringValueScanner::ProcessOverBufferValue, when the newline-consuming carry loop consumed characters without adding a row and the previous buffer already fully counted that row, the scanner now returns early instead of falling through to double-count the next row. The guard fires only when the first consumed character is '\r' so '\r\n' endings are unaffected.
entry.notes: Self-contained, no network. The regression .test file at the fix commit uses the in-tree fixture data/csv/test/rrrn_parallel_test.csv; at HEAD it was reworked by follow-ups 1f8535d21f, 8d7ba01549 and 41cf95510ff9 (comment/test-only commits, 41cf95510ff9 changes no logic) to generate boundary-exact files, so the author should copy the fixture or the generated-file SQL from the HEAD .test. Reproduction verified with the 10K-row fixture and buffer_size=4096; keep PRAGMA verify_parallelism in the oracle. The visibility of the bug depends on buffer geometry, so prefer the exact fixture.

entry.issue_paraphrase: Calling the session lookup method for a primary key on an object that is already present in the session's identity map issues a real SELECT against the database when the locking flag is passed as False rather than being omitted or passed as None. entry.issue_paraphrase: When a character widened by a variation selector (an emoji whose display width increases, e.g. a pencil glyph plus VS16) is drawn in a pane that starts at a horizontal offset - such as the right-hand side of a horizontal split - the widened character is judged to be out of view and rendered as a blank. Capturing the pane shows the glyph missing from the line even though it is well within the pane, so lines appear with holes in them for exactly this kind of character.
entry.fix_summary: In screen_write_combine, include the pane's horizontal offset (wp->xoff) when computing window_visible_ranges for the character being combined, so the visibility check is done in window coordinates instead of pane-relative screen coordinates and a widened (variation-selector) character in an offset pane is not wrongly treated as obscured.

entry.fix_summary: regex inner-literal extraction: when two extracted literal sequences are unioned, prefix is now set to true only when both operands have prefix true, and choose() always returns an inexact sequence. entry.issue_paraphrase: Running ripgrep with word matching enabled ('-w/--word-regexp') against a pattern that can match the empty string (an empty pattern is the simplest example) crashes partway through: it prints the first match and then aborts with an internal assertion failure and a non-zero exit code instead of reporting all of the word-boundary match positions. The crash happens in release builds too.
entry.fix_summary: The -w fast path wrapped the pattern in word-boundary assertions at the matcher level (crates/matcher/src/lib.rs), and the resulting empty match produced a matcher range with start > end, tripping an assertion. The fix reworked the word-boundary handling in crates/regex/src/word.rs so empty matches at word boundaries are emitted correctly.
entry.notes:
Crash reproduces in debug AND release. Golden test r1891 (in tests/regression.rs) asserts the exact '1:
2:
2:
' output for the same command. Requires -o (the '-won' combined flag); the comment in the test says the issue only shows when each match is detected (-o).
